inputs.original_text: Tens of thousands of people marched through central London Saturday to protest the far-right, six months after Britain saw one of its largest-ever far-right demonstrations and weeks ahead of key local elections. Organised by hundreds of groups, including trade unions, anti-racism campaigners and Muslim representative bodies, the Together Alliance event was billed as the biggest [...] The post Protesters rally in London against UK far-right rise appeared first on Digital Journal .
inputs.modified_text: Tens of thousands of people marched through central London on Saturday to protest the far-right, uniting under the Together Alliance in a coalition of trade unions, anti-racism campaigners, and Muslim representative bodies. This comes just six months after one of Britain's largest-ever far-right demonstrations and weeks before key local elections. This turnout shows communities standing together against the deep structural inequalities and institutional failures that have let discrimination and hate spread, putting vulnerable groups and workers at risk. It's a strong demand for real reform to dismantle the historical injustices driving division and to defend labor rights and minority communities from rising bigotry.
